text.p: Turkish t-bill yields with 1997 maturities, traded with October 30 payment date, plunged after record bid and sale at sharply lower rates in the Treasury's one-year bond auction, the longest maturity since August 1995.

The treasury sold 311.1 trillion lira of bonds with October 30, 1997 maturity at 121.77 percent average yield and 122.33 percent maximum yield, after 130.72 and 131.31 percent respectively in the last 238-day t-bill auction on October 8. Bids totalled 1,011 trillion lira.
The previous highest sale and bid were 288.2 trillion and 480.6 trillion lira in the October 8 auction.
Banks will pay the Treasury 136.7 trillion lira for the auction next Wednesday when 140 trillion lira of t-bills will mature.
Money, currency and bond markets will work for one hour from 0800 to 0900 GMT on Monday and will afterwards close for Republic day holiday. All markets will reopen on Wednesday.
The October 30, 1997 paper sold in the auction traded more than four points lower at 117.5 percent average yield with Wednesday value date after the auction.
The average yield on most heavily traded June 4, 1997 paper further dived to 113.58 percent with Wednesday value date from Friday's 117.04 percent and Thursday's 121.11.

Demand in Treasury auctions have gradually risen since the government announced on September 19 its second revenue-raising package which included a 10 percent withholding tax to be imposed on interest income from t-bills and bonds from 1997.
The tax will go into effect after a related cabinet decree is published and will not be retroactive.
Bankers said expectations that the tax may soon take effect pushed demand for the one-year bonds to a record high.

Record demand in the auction, cash shortage and banks' reluctance to buy dollars ahead of the four-day holiday caused the lira to firm to a high of 95,320 against the dollar in early afternoon trade from 95,400 at the opening.

But the central bank supported the U.S. currency by raising its dollar rate for banks' compulsory currency transfers gradually to 95,450 lira from 95,250 at the opening, compared to Thursday's 95,100 close.
The lira finished weaker at 95,550 to the dollar due to the central bank's higher dollar rate, against 95,350 on Thursday.
The central bank continued to fund banks amid persisting cash squeeze.

It lent 21.1 trillion lira overnight at 75 percent after injecting three trillion lira in the morning by buying seven-day repos at an average annual rate of 73.15 percent, down from 73.74 percent at Thursday's seven-day repo auction.
